baseline.name: Scan each queried range
baseline.approach: Count matching values directly between left and right for every query.
baseline.time: O(w) per query of width w; O(q*n) worst case across q queries
baseline.space: O(1) working space while retaining input

archived.name: Per-value sorted index lists
archived.time: O(n+V) build; O(log(f+1)) query with O(1) handling when the value is absent, where f is its stored frequency

why: Two binary searches locate the queried value's positions in the requested range without examining each range element.
quantitative_comparison: A width-w query inspects w values in the baseline; the archive does two logarithmic index-list searches after preprocessing. Overall benefit depends on query count and range widths relative to the O(n+V) setup cost.
tradeoffs: Uses additional stored positions and a fixed value domain. One tiny query may not justify preprocessing; updates would require maintaining the index lists. No measured crossover or speedup is available.
evidence_basis: Static preprocessing/query-cost model from the captured source; no benchmark.
